findings.title: BOLA — Cross-user data access via /vehicles/1

differential_analysis.similarity_analysis: Similarity score 100.00% — requester received near-identical data to owner's resource
differential_analysis.ownership_analysis: Response contains owner's identifying fields: ['owner_id=1', 'id=1'] — requester received another user's data
differential_analysis.summary: Differential analysis: similarity=100.00%, ownership_mismatch=True, sensitive_fields=2, confidence=Critical

findings.description: Endpoint /vehicles/1 returns data to any authenticated user regardless of resource ownership. User B accessed an object belonging to User A without authorization check.
findings.remediation: Implement object-level authorization. Before returning any resource, verify: does the requesting user own this object? Return HTTP 403 if ownership check fails.

findings.title: Broken Auth — /v1/vehicles returns data without authentication

evidence.actual: 200 OK — JSON data returned without token
evidence.note: Confirmed real endpoint — not a guessed path

findings.description: Endpoint /v1/vehicles returns data to unauthenticated requests. No Authorization header required. T-Mobile 2023 breach pattern: unauthenticated endpoints exposed 37 million customer records.
findings.remediation: Add authentication middleware to this endpoint. Return HTTP 401 for all requests without a valid token.

findings.title: Broken Auth / Misconfig — /health exposes credentials without auth
findings.description: Health endpoint /health exposes internal credentials without authentication.
findings.remediation: Remove all sensitive data from health endpoints. Return only {status: ok}.

findings.title: Broken Auth — JWT has no expiry claim
findings.description: JWT tokens never expire — stolen tokens valid forever.
findings.remediation: Add exp claim. Set expiry to 15-60 minutes.

findings.title: Broken Auth — JWT 'None' Algorithm Attack Successful
findings.description: API accepts JWT with 'none' algorithm — signature bypassed.
findings.remediation: Whitelist allowed algorithms. Reject 'none'.

findings.title: Broken Auth — No brute force protection on login
findings.description: Login allows unlimited failed attempts — credential stuffing possible.
findings.remediation: Rate limit: block after 5 failures per IP. Add exponential backoff.

findings.title: Excessive Exposure — /admin/users returns sensitive fields

evidence.note: Fields present in response that should never be exposed via API

findings.description: Endpoint /admin/users returns sensitive internal fields: password. These should never be exposed in API responses.
findings.remediation: Define explicit response allowlists. Strip sensitive fields before returning data. Use separate DTOs for internal vs external representations.

findings.title: Unrestricted Resource Consumption — no rate limiting

evidence.expected: 429 Too Many Requests after a threshold

findings.description: The endpoint /auth/profile served 30 rapid requests with no throttling (no HTTP 429). This permits scraping, brute force, and denial-of-service by resource exhaustion.
findings.remediation: Apply per-user/per-IP rate limiting at the gateway or middleware.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoint
findings.description: Login endpoint allows unlimited attempts, enabling credential stuffing and brute force attacks.
findings.remediation: Block or delay after 5 failed attempts per IP/account. Implement CAPTCHA and account lockout policies.

findings.title: BFLA — Regular user invoked privileged function
findings.description: The endpoint GET /admin/users appears to expose a privileged/administrative function, yet a standard user token receives a successful response. Function-level authorization is not enforced.
findings.remediation: Enforce role/permission checks on privileged endpoints server-side. Reject non-privileged callers with HTTP 403 regardless of endpoint knowledge.

findings.title: Business Flow Abuse — repeatable sensitive action
findings.description: The sensitive business action POST /payments/process succeeded 5/5 times on repeated submission of the same input, indicating no redemption / idempotency / anti-automation control (e.g. a coupon reusable indefinitely).
findings.remediation: Track single-use tokens/redemptions server-side; add anti-automation controls.

findings.title: Business Flow Abuse — negative value accepted
findings.description: The endpoint POST /payments/process accepted a negative quantity/amount, which can invert a business transaction (e.g. a credit instead of a charge).
findings.remediation: Validate numeric business inputs server-side; reject non-positive values.
findings.verification_note: No verifier available — accepted by default

findings.title: Security Misconfiguration — Sensitive data at /health
findings.description: Endpoint /health publicly exposes sensitive configuration data including: secret, key, database, debug, admin
findings.remediation: Disable or restrict access to debug/health endpoints in production. Never expose credentials, secrets, or internal config publicly.

findings.title: Security Misconfiguration — Wildcard CORS origin
findings.description:
CORS is configured to allow all origins (*).
Any website can make cross-origin requests to this API.
findings.remediation: Restrict CORS to specific trusted origins. Never use wildcard (*) with credentials. Validate Origin header against an allowlist.

findings.title: Security Misconfiguration — Missing security headers
findings.description: Security headers missing: X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-XSS-Protection
findings.remediation: Add all recommended security headers. Use helmet.js (Node) or equivalent middleware.

findings.title: Improper Inventory — API documentation exposed without auth
findings.description: API documentation/spec at /redoc is reachable without authentication.
findings.remediation: Restrict or remove documentation endpoints in production.
findings.verification_note: No verifier available — accepted by default

findings.title: Improper Inventory — multiple live API versions
findings.description: Multiple API versions are exposed simultaneously (v1, v2); older versions often lack the security controls of the current one.
findings.remediation: Retire deprecated versions; inventory and gate all exposed versions.
